title: A Phase I/II Study to Learn About the Safety and Effects of a New Medicine Called IPN60350 Alone or in Combination With Other Anticancer Therapies in Adults With Locally Advanced or Metastatic Solid Tumors
official: An Open-label Phase I/II, Dose Escalation, Dose Optimization, and Dose Expansion Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetic, Pharmacodynamic, Immunogenicity, and Antitumor Activity of IPN60350 as Monotherapy or in Combination With Other Anticancer Therapies in Adult Participants With Locally Advanced or Metastatic Solid Tumors
summary:
The purpose of this study is to learn about the safety of a new medicine called IPN60350 and how the body responds to it. Researchers will also look for early signs of antitumor activity in adults with locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors.

All participants in this study will receive IPN60350, either alone or in combination with other anticancer therapies.

The study has two parts.

* Phase Ia (dose escalation) will test IPN60350 at different dose levels to learn which doses are safe and can be given in future parts of the study.
* Phase Ib (dose optimization and expansion) will test one or more selected dose levels in a larger number of participants. This will help researchers better understand the safety of IPN60350 and whether it shows early signs of antitumor activity in different tumor types.

Each part will consist of the following periods:

* A screening period (up to 28 days) to assess whether the participant can take part, requiring at least 1 visit to the study center.
* A treatment period where IPN60350 is administered in repeating treatment cycles.

The study includes health assessments, blood tests, tissue samples (biopsies), and imaging scans to help researchers better understand the safety of IPN60350 and its potential effects on tumors.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Participant must be ≥18 years of age, at the time of signing the informed consent.
* Histologically or cytologically confirmed locally advanced/metastatic solid tumors.
* Have at least 1 measurable disease per RECIST version 1.1.
* Participants with solid tumors who have:

  * Relapsed or refractory disease after receiving at least 1 prior therapy known to provide clinical benefit for their disease based on locally approved standard of care; AND
  * No remaining available approved therapy; or for whom locally approved standard therapies are contraindicated or not deemed appropriate by the treating investigator.
* Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0 to 1.
* Contraceptive use by men or women should be consistent with local regulations regarding the methods of contraception for those participating in clinical studies.
* Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) \>50%.
* Adequate bone marrow function.
* Adequate hepatic function and absence of laboratory abnormalities indicating hepatic injury before first dose of study intervention.
* Adequate renal function before first dose of study intervention.
* Prothrombin time (PT) or international normalized ratio (INR) ≤1.5× upper limit of normal (ULN).
* At the time of screening, a tumor tissue specimen is required for enrollment into phase Ia and phase Ib parts of the study.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Known second malignancy either progressing or requiring active treatment.
* Has not recovered (i.e., to CTCAE version 6.0 Grade 1 or to baseline) from previous anticancer therapy-induced AEs. Note: Grade ≤2 AEs with no impact on participant safety are exceptions to this criterion and may qualify for the study, e.g., Grade ≤2 hair loss or stable peripheral neuropathy.
* Major surgery before receiving the first dose of study treatment. Participants must have adequate wound healing and have recovered from surgery related complications/toxicities prior to first dose.
* Active brain metastases or leptomeningeal metastases.
* Significant concurrent, uncontrolled medical condition that would put participants at unacceptable risk from study participation or preclude them from complying with study procedures as per investigator assessment, including, but not limited to renal, hepatic, hematological, gastrointestinal, endocrine, pulmonary, neurological, cerebral, or psychiatric disease.
* History of (non-infectious) interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis that required steroids, current ILD/pneumonitis, or where suspected ILD/pneumonitis cannot be ruled out by imaging screening.
* Clinically significant pulmonary disease that may increase the risk of drug-related pneumonitis, including but not limited to pulmonary fibrosis, severe or uncontrolled chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), uncontrolled asthma, or ongoing pulmonary infection.
* Participants with uncontrolled human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). HIV-infected participants are eligible if they meet criteria specified in protocol.
* Known active infection with hepatitis B virus (HBV) OR hepatitis C virus (HCV). Participants are eligible if they meet criteria described in the protocol.
* History of allogeneic organ transplantation or graft-versus-host disease.
* Known hypersensitivity to study drug, other monoclonal antibodies, or any of the excipients including sensitivity to heparin or heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.
* Clinically significant cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease including but not limited to acute myocardial infarction, unstable or severe angina pectoris, endoscopic or open-heart cardiac surgery, stroke, transient ischemic attack, cerebral hemorrhage, or cerebral infarction, congestive heart failure, arrhythmia, or uncontrolled hypertension.

Note: Additional protocol specified inclusion/exclusion criteria may apply.
